mutations.label: the OOS envelope loses its XML declaration, which is the half of the recording a reader would assume rather than check: Scaleway has none, so copying Scaleway here looks right and is wrong

the OOS branch falls through to the Exoscale one, so Resource is omitted instead of present-and-empty and a BucketName appears that the producer does not send: the single likeliest shortcut, since the two dialects agree on the final period and the declaration
the two response identifiers are derived apart, where the recorded answer carried the same value in x-amz-id-2 and x-amz-request-id

a fourth shape is admitted by range rather than by name, so adding a constant without an envelope ships a provider whose errors are whatever the default branch happens to render (the constructor's allow-list, asserted by TestUploadHeaderValidationAndConstructor)

note: The subject is the OOS door of #850, and the envelope it answers for an absent bucket. Outscale's OOS is S3 — octl storage api lists S3's own operation names, and osc-sdk-go's pkg/oos is built on aws-sdk-go-v2/service/s3 with smithy errors — so there was no proprietary dialect to invent. There WAS an envelope to measure, and the three differences from its neighbours are exactly what no reading of a document would have produced: <Resource> present and EMPTY where Scaleway fills it and Exoscale omits it, NO <BucketName> where both others carry it, and one identifier answered in both x-amz-id-2 and x-amz-request-id where the others derive them apart. Recorded by an anonymous GET on a name that does not exist (docs/evidence/outscale-oos-missing-bucket.json), which sends no signature, is attributed to no account, creates nothing and is billed to nobody: the user's account was offered for this and deliberately not used. The first two mutations are the shortcuts a maintainer would actually take — drop the declaration because Scaleway has none, or let the branch fall through to Exoscale because the two agree on the period — and both are caught by comparing the emitted envelope against the recording rather than against a hand-written expectation. The fourth leaves the two dialect branches alone and widens the constructor's allow-list instead, because a range check there is how a fourth provider would ship with whatever the default branch renders.
